arxiv-1902-08830.title: Categorization in the Wild: Generalizing Cognitive Models to Naturalistic Data across Languages
arxiv-1902-08830.creator: Lea Frermann, Mirella Lapata
arxiv-1902-08830.description: Abstract Categories such as animal or furniture are acquired at an early age and play an important role in processing, organizing, and communicating world knowledge. Categories exist across cultures: they allow to efficiently represent the complexity of the world, and members of a community strongly agree on their nature, revealing a shared mental representation.

arxiv-2311-04158.description: Abstract Recent works in dimensionality reduction for regression tasks have introduced the notion of sensitivity, an estimate of the importance of a specific datapoint in a dataset, offering provable guarantees on the quality of the approximation after removing low-sensitivity datapoints via subsampling.

arxiv-2404-10532.title: Macdonald Identities, Weyl–Kac Denominator Formulas and Affine Grassmannian Elements
arxiv-2404-10532.creator: Cédric LECOUVEY and David WAHICHE
arxiv-2404-10532.description: Abstract The Nekrasov–Okounkov formula gives an expression for the Fourier coefficients of the Euler functions as a sum of hook length products. This formula can be deduced from a specialization in a renormalization of the affine type A A Weyl denominator formula and the use of a polynomial argument.

arxiv-2409-10555.title: Convolutional Networks as Extremely Small Foundation Models: Visual Prompting and Theoretical Perspective
arxiv-2409-10555.creator: Jianqiao Wangni Tsinghua University Beijing, China zjnqha@gmail.com
arxiv-2409-10555.description: Abstract Comparing to deep neural networks trained for specific tasks, those foundational deep networks trained on generic datasets such as ImageNet classification, benefits from larger-scale datasets, simpler network structure and easier training techniques. In this paper, we design a prompting module which performs few-shot adaptation of generic deep networks to new tasks.

pmc-10558580.title: Distinct and targetable role of calcium-sensing receptor in leukaemia
pmc-10558580.creator: Raquel S. Pereira, Rahul Kumar, Alessia Cais, Lara Paulini, Alisa Kahler, Jimena Bravo, Valentina R. Minciacchi, Theresa Krack, Eric Kowarz, Costanza Zanetti, Parimala Sonika Godavarthy, Fabian Hoeller, Pablo Llavona, Tabea Stark, Georg Tascher, Daniel Nowak, Eshwar Meduri, Brian J. P. Huntly, Chris
pmc-10558580.description: Haematopoietic stem cells (HSC) reside in the bone marrow microenvironment (BMM), where they respond to extracellular calcium [eCa2+] via the G-protein coupled calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR). Here we show that a calcium gradient exists in this BMM, and that [eCa2+] and response to [eCa2+] differ between leukaemias.

pmc-10749441.title: Antifungal Effect of Probiotic Lactobacillus casei on Drug-Resistant Oral Candida albicans Isolated from Patients with Hematological Malignancy: an in vitro Study
pmc-10749441.creator: Seyedeh Saba Sharifzadeh, Ensieh Lotfali, Simin Lesan, Taraneh Farrokhnia
pmc-10749441.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Statement of the Problem: Candida albicans (C. albicans) is recognized as the most common opportunistic pathogen in patients with an impaired immune system, and due to the frequent use of antifungal medicine, a variety of drug-resistant species are developing. Probiotics are a part of the human microbiome and natural competitors of Candida by producing lactic acid, low pH, and other secreted metabolites.

pmc-11728085.title: The REGENERATE Study: A Non-Randomized Feasibility Study of an Intervention to REduce anticholinerGic burdEN in oldER pATiEnts
pmc-11728085.creator: Athagran Nakham, Christine Bond, Moira Cruickshank, Rumana Newlands, Phyo Kyaw Myint
pmc-11728085.description: Background: Anticholinergic burden (ACB) from medications has been associated with adverse outcomes in older adults. Aim: The aim was to conduct a non-randomized feasibility study of an intervention to reduce the anticholinergic burden in older patients (REGENERATE) to inform a subsequent definitive trial.

pmc-12534610.title: Unicorn: U-Net for sea ice forecasting with convolutional neural ordinary differential equations
pmc-12534610.creator: Jaesung Park, Yoonseo Cho, Jong-June Jeon, Jinku Park, Hyun-Cheol Kim, Sungchul Hong
pmc-12534610.description: Sea ice at the North Pole is vital to global climate dynamics. However, accurately forecasting sea ice poses a significant challenge due to the intricate interaction among multiple variables. Leveraging the capability to integrate multiple inputs and powerful performances seamlessly, many studies have turned to neural networks for sea ice forecasting.

pmc-12748022.title: Expansion of cagA Copy Number in Helicobacter pylori During Co‐Infection in a Mouse Model
pmc-12748022.creator: Kavinda Tissera, Ashansa Ramanayake, Myeong‐A Kim, Eui‐Jeong Noh, Sacheera Angulmaduwa, Dowon Seo, Yong‐Joon Cho, Jeong‐Heon Cha
pmc-12748022.description: IntroductionThe virulence factor CagA is critical in mediating inflammation, and Helicobacter pylori PMSS1 dynamically modulates cagA copy number in response to host immune pressure. Co‐infection with Salmonella enterica serotype Typhimurium has been shown to heighten systemic inflammation and reduce H. pylori colonization while maintaining type IV secretion system functionality.

pmc-12804315.title: Comparative Study of [18F]DPA714 and [18F]FDG PET Tracers in an Experimental Model of Pulmonary Tuberculosis
pmc-12804315.creator: M. A. Stammes, M. P. M. Vierboom, C. C. Sombroek, J. Bakker, L. Meijer, R. A. W. Vervenne, S. O. Hofman, E. Nutma, I. Kondova, A. D. Windhorst, J. A. M. Langermans, F. A. W. Verreck
pmc-12804315.description: PurposeTuberculosis (TB) continues to afflict global health. Therefore, a deeper understanding of the host response mechanisms that underly pathogenesis versus disease control upon infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) is required to leverage the development of improved therapeutic or prophylactic TB treatment regimens.

pmc-13285962.title: Proteomic Mendelian randomization and machine learning reveal causal plasma biomarkers in cardiorenal comorbidity

pmc-13302252.title: Impaired alert tone perception and post-MRI malfunction in patients with S-ICD: a three-center analysis
pmc-13302252.creator: J Woermann, C Hausmann, Y Bocchini, T Fink, S Jurisic, A Breitenstein, P Sommer, V Sciacca, S Dittrich, J Grobecker, T Maximidou, J Ackmann, J Schipper, D Steven, J Lueker
pmc-13302252.description: BackgroundThe subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (S-ICD) provides audible alert tones to indicate device or lead issues. Impaired perception of this warning tone or functional loss after magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) may compromise patient safety.PurposeThis study investigated (1) factors associated with inability of patients to perceive the alert tone, and (2) the impact of MRI scans on post-scan tone function.

pmc-13333920.title: ASO-functionalized gold nanoparticles for gene silencing in drug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa: a proof-of-concept study
pmc-13333920.creator: Sarah Najah AlJanabi, Maroua Gdoura-Ben Amor, Wathiq Abbas Al-Draghi, Hanen Sellami, Olfa Frikha-Gargouri
pmc-13333920.description: The present work aims at evaluating a novel therapeutic technique against clinical samples of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a multiple drug resistant bacterium by integrating gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) with antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) (ASO-AuNPs) to target and silence the blaVIM and blaCTX-M genes.

pmc-13376167.title: Cell death modalities modulate inflammatory and regenerative programs in zebrafish sensory organs
pmc-13376167.creator: Daniela Münch, Shiyuan Chen, Elizabeth Ellis, Nicolas Denans, Mark E. Lush, Kaitlyn Petentler, Jose E. Javier, KyeongMin Bae, Tatjana Piotrowski
pmc-13376167.description: Regeneration is triggered by cells dying due to various types of injuries. However, it remains unclear whether different types of cell death elicit distinct regeneration responses. Here, we systematically profile dynamic transcriptional responses of macrophages and lateral line cells to different cell death modalities during zebrafish sensory hair cell regeneration.

pmc-13578057.title: The environmental impact of diagnostic imaging: opportunities for pediatric radiologists
pmc-13578057.creator: Jonathan Gross, Sumit Pruthi, Reed A Omary, Elizabeth J Snyder
pmc-13578057.description: Healthcare operations are a major contributor to human-produced greenhouse gas emissions worldwide and in the USA in particular. Medical imaging, largely due to its high energy use requirements, disproportionately contributes to healthcare’s negative environmental impacts. Although there has been growing concern about radiology’s role in climate change, most existing knowledge of radiology’s impact derives from adult radiology departments.
